newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs around steady - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs around steady - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices were around steady early Monday with cooler weather in most areas boosting movement but a pick-up in demand also was noted, livestock dealers and packer buyers said.
"We've have good movement so far and we're expecting to get more hogs this week (than last week) with the cooler weather but there is also decent demand," one Indiana-based dealer said.
He noted light early trade in the country at $57.00 and at plants at $58.50 per cwt. USDA reported an Indiana/Ohio plant top on Friday of $59.00.
In southern Minnesota there a few hogs were trading early at $56.50 per cwt directly to plants, which was around $0.50 lower than prices paid for similar hogs in the same area on Friday.
"We have good movement," one dealer said. He noted, however, that only a few hogs had been bought at the lower values and the market may end up steady.
Fewer hogs were reported to be moving in Illinois where some expected the market to be steady to $0.50 higher.
"We've got pretty slow movement and a bit more demand," one Illinois dealer said.
